claims.statement: createGitHubWebhookRoutes is mounted at /github/webhook before express.json() in packages/server/src/index.ts because the X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC authenticates exact wire bytes; the router applies a 60 req/min rate limiter then express.raw with a 256kb cap so req.body stays a Buffer, and the handler rejects non-Buffer bodies with 400 GITHUB_WEBHOOK_RAW_BODY_REQUIRED and returns 503 GITHUB_WEBHOOK_UNCONFIGURED when GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset.

Signature verification requires the X-Hub-Signature-256 header to match ^sha256=[a-f0-9]{64}$ and compares the HMAC-sha256 of the raw body against it with crypto.timingSafeEqual (constant-time), rejecting with 401 GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID.

Repository allowlist: configuredRepository() parses GITHUB_REPOSITORY_PATHS as JSON mapping repository full_name to local paths, accepting only absolute, existing directories and returning the realpathSync-resolved path; any failure yields 422 GITHUB_WEBHOOK_REPOSITORY_UNCONFIGURED.

The issues branch only accepts actions opened and labeled (zod issuePayload); a labeled event is ignored with 202 label_not_selected unless the label equals GITHUB_LOOP_LABEL (default djimitflo), and unsupported X-GitHub-Event types get 202 ignored/unsupported_event.

Issue intake imports exactly one triaged work item via IntegrationInboxService.importEvent (source github_issue, recommended_loop repo-maintenance-loop, value_score default 85 for github_issue), wraps issue content in a BEGIN_EXTERNAL_CONTENT trust=untrusted fence as a prompt-injection defense, derives risk_class from labels (critical/sev1/p0→critical, high/sev2/p1→high, medium/p2→medium, else low), and responds execution_started: false with operator_review_required: true — the connector never starts goals, loops, or workers for issues.

Re-delivery of the same issue under a new delivery ID goes through WorkItemService.upsertBySourceRef, which refreshes title/description/metadata and only raises risk_class while preserving operator-owned state (status, assigned_runtime, assigned_agent_id, parent_goal_id, recommended_loop).

The pull_request branch (actions opened/synchronize/reopened) runs a single immediate SQLite transaction that creates a goal with the untrusted-content-wrapped objective, starts a repo-maintenance-loop run whose target_finding file_path is a stable anchor file (first present of package.json/README.md/AGENTS.md, else 422 GITHUB_WEBHOOK_NO_ANCHOR_FILE), and records the delivery; GithubPrReviewService.startReview is called only after the transaction commits because shelling to gh must never happen inside it.

Every processed delivery is persisted in github_webhook_deliveries (id, event, source_ref, result_json, payload_sha256) keyed by the X-GitHub-Delivery header; an identical redelivery replays the stored response with 200 status duplicate, while a delivery ID rebound to different event/source_ref/payload hash or missing result yields 409 GITHUB_WEBHOOK_DELIVERY_CONFLICT.

GithubPrReviewService maintains github_pull_request_reviews with a unique index on (owner, repo, pr_number, head_sha) and status pending/commented/completed/failed; startReview never throws — gh or GitHub failures are recorded as status failed with a github_pr_review_failed audit entry and the webhook still answers 202, keeping the local DB authoritative.

Phase 1 (default, no LLM) synthesizes an already-completed manual maker lease (the PR's commits are the patch, no worktree) and a manual checker lease driving the real LoopService.submitCheckerVerdict with a manual_attestation; the verdict is a rule-based stub over gh pr view stats — >40 files or >1500 changed lines or paths matching /.env|secret|credential/i yield needs_revision, otherwise accepted. The worktree-less review run's worktree/diff verification gates legitimately fail on the synthetic lease, but once the verdict is posted settleReviewRun flips the run (running or blocked) to completed with metadata.settled_by='github-pr-review' and idempotently completes the still-running goals of all settled review runs — the GitHub-posted verdict is computed independently from the PR's own diff stats either way.

Phase 2 (opt-in via GITHUB_PR_REVIEW_RUNTIME set to codex/opencode/claude/gemini/editor/mock) returns pending immediately and asynchronously fetches pull/<n>/head, materializes a real worktree on a djimitflo/pr-review branch reset to the head SHA, writes gh pr diff into .djimitflo/PR_REVIEW_PACKET.md wrapped as untrusted external content, and drives a real checker through LoopService.executeChecker with a 480s timeout; on success it posts the comment and settles the run via settleReviewRun like Phase 1, and it is off by default to avoid auto-spawning paid LLM calls on every PR push.

postToGithub writes the markdown comment (verdict line, diff stats, loop run ID, optional roborev static-findings section matched on owner/repo at head SHA) to a temp file posted via gh pr comment --body-file, then sets a Commit Status via gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/statuses/{head_sha} with context djimitflo-review because the Checks API rejects personal-access-token auth with a hard 403; all gh calls use a 15s timeout.

Because GithubPrReviewService shells out to gh for PR comments and commit statuses, the production Dockerfile runner stage installs the OS packages ca-certificates, git, python3-minimal, curl, procps, and libatomic1 via apt (L64-L67, under a retry- and IPv4-bounded apt config added after repeated Debian-mirror build stalls), then installs the GitHub CLI from a statically fetched, pinned .deb — ARG GH_CLI_VERSION=2.100.0, downloaded via retry-bounded curl from github.com/cli/cli/releases for the dpkg build architecture, installed with dpkg -i, and verified with gh --version at build time (L69-L77) — rather than adding a third-party apt repository; an inline comment names GithubPrReviewService as the consumer.

After the loop daemon's verification pass finds all gates passing (step 9b), it calls LoopDraftPrService.openForRun for the certified run; the call is wrapped so a PR failure never fails the daemon, and the service itself returns null unless LOOP_AUTO_DRAFT_PR_ENABLED is exactly 'true' and GITHUB_REPOSITORY/GITHUB_TOKEN are set, keeping the GitHub-publishing hand-off opt-in by default.

LoopDraftPrService opens at most one draft PR per run: it only acts on loop_runs in status ready_for_human_merge or completed, returns the already-recorded loop_runs.metadata.pr_url unchanged when present, and converts every missing precondition or GitHub failure into a draft_pr_failed warning loop event with a null return instead of throwing.

The draft-PR push commits only the maker's real files from the latest non-superseded completed maker lease's worktree — tracked diffs plus untracked files, excluding node_modules content, symlinks, and lockfile install noise (a package-lock.json whose sibling package.json was untouched) — failing with 'no changes in the maker worktree' if nothing qualifies, and authenticates the push with the token as a one-off http.extraheader basic-auth header so the token is never written to the remote URL or .git/config and is scrubbed from any recorded error message.

The draft PR is opened via POST /repos/{GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pulls with draft: true, a 'loop:'-prefixed title taken from the linked self-improvement proposal when the goal has one, base branch LOOP_DRAFT_PR_BASE (default main), push remote LOOP_DRAFT_PR_REMOTE (default origin), and a body listing the recorded checker/security_checker verdicts and the file list; on success the PR URL is persisted into loop_runs.metadata.pr_url (at most one PR per run) and a draft_pr_opened loop event is recorded.

Before pushing, openForRun applies two optional gates: Batch-8 evidence freshness (LOOP_EVIDENCE_FRESHNESS_MODE, default off) re-fingerprints the maker lease's evidence_read_set against FETCH_HEAD of the base branch — shadow records evidence_stale_shadow but opens anyway, enforce records evidence_stale with metadata.evidence_freshness.requeue=true and does not open, and a failed fetch fails open as 'unknown' — and the RX-6 arrival throttle (LOOP_DRAFT_PR_THROTTLE_MODE) counts open 'loop:' PRs and at or above LOOP_DRAFT_PR_MAX_OPEN (default 5) records draft_pr_throttled (enforce, opens nothing) or draft_pr_throttle_shadow (shadow, opens anyway), failing open when the open-PR list call fails.

The draft PR begins the merge-survival fitness measurement: merge-survival.ts (MERGE_SURVIVAL_ENABLED, default off) polls every loop_runs.metadata.pr_url read-only and settles it exactly once — closed unmerged is failure; merged counts success only when at least MERGE_SURVIVAL_MIN_RETAINED (default 0.5) of the PR's added lines remain on main after SURVIVAL_DAYS (14 days) — landing as a skill outcome (domain 'merge') for the maker species; listDraftPrs/countOpenLoopPrs expose the same metadata with no GitHub call.
